topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: The Hook: Defining the Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A bead slides down a wire from point A to point B under gravity. Which path takes the shortest time? Contrast the intuitive 'straight line' against the 'curved path' using a split-screen animation.
sections.example: Compare a roller coaster designer choosing a straight slope versus a curved 'drop' to reach the bottom fastest.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Energy vs. Time
sections.content: Briefly review Conservation of Energy (v = sqrt(2gh)). Explain why the path is not just about distance (the straight line), but about speed (gaining height early to maximize velocity).
sections.example: Visual graph showing how a steeper initial drop increases velocity earlier, even if the total path distance is longer.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
sections.content: Reveal the Brachistochrone curve: The Cycloid. Visualize it as the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling circle. Use an animation overlaying a cycloid path on a grid to show the 'accelerate, then cruise' strategy.
sections.example: An animation of a wheel rolling along a ceiling, with a highlighted red dot marking the cycloid trajectory from A to B.

sections.title: Conceptual Insight: Why it Works
sections.content: Explain the balance: The cycloid optimizes the trade-off between path length and gravitational acceleration. It 'steals' speed by dropping vertically, then levels off to utilize that speed.
sections.example: Compare a cheetah (which accelerates rapidly) to a marathon runner; the cycloid is the 'cheetah' of geometric paths.

sections.title: Summary & Real-world Application
sections.content: Conclude with the Brachistochrone's legacy in the Calculus of Variations. Mention the Tautochrone property (the curve where time is independent of starting position).
sections.example: Visualizing how this principle is used in high-speed rail track design and water-slide engineering for optimal transit times.
